answer:
Let last month’s monthly growth rate be \(8\%=0.08\).

| Interpretation | New monthly growth rate | Next subscriber count from 800 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Relative increase: “25% better than 8%” means \(8\%\times 1.25\) | \(10\%\) | \(800(1.10)=880\) |
| Percentage-point increase: “25%” added to the rate means \(8\%+25\%\) | \(33\%\) | \(800(1.33)=1064\) |

To double within 6 months, the monthly rate must satisfy  
\[
(1+r)^6\ge 2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad r\ge 2^{1/6}-1\approx 12.25\%.
\]

- At \(10\%\) monthly: after 6 months, \(800(1.10)^6\approx 1,417\), or even after 7 months, \(800(1.10)^7\approx 1,559\), so it does **not** reach 1,600.
- At \(33\%\) monthly: \(800(1.33)^6\approx 4,428\), so it easily exceeds 1,600.

**Conclusion:** The \(10\%\) reading is the relative-increase interpretation; the \(33\%\) reading is the percentage-point interpretation. Only the **33% monthly growth** reading could double an 800-person audience within six further months.
